user_story: As a user, I want ProsePal to open into the writing experience so I can start without choosing between product implementations.
expected_behaviour: The app scene constructs MomentAppRootView with the shared writing service, account model, SwiftData container, and Write/Drafts/Settings tabs.
compatibility_notes: The app presents one current ProsePal experience; historical implementation distinctions are not user-facing product vocabulary.

user_story: As a first-time user, I want a short welcome before the Moment sheet so I understand the app without being blocked by sign-in or purchase.
expected_behaviour: Welcome state controls whether the welcome or Moment tabs appear; welcome can be dismissed into the writing experience.
compatibility_notes: Welcome must not become a marketing splash on every launch.

user_story: As a user, I want to start with who the message is for so the app frames the moment around a person.
expected_behaviour: MomentInput stores trimmed personName; MomentSheetView shows the person field before relationship, occasion, and optional detail.
compatibility_notes: At least two non-whitespace characters are required; pre-commit layout stability remains US-004.

user_story: As a user typing a name, I want the layout to stay stable until I submit or leave the person field.
expected_behaviour: Typing a person keeps the uncommitted header and setup sections visible; submitting commits the person and switches to the named Moment setup.
external_evidence_remaining: Direct running-app coverage of the layout before and after person-field commit remains absent.
compatibility_notes: Do not overstate the current XCUITest as direct pre-commit layout coverage.
MomentSheetView bases active layout and header controls on committed-person state.

user_story: As a user, I want to choose the relationship naturally so the draft can respect context.
expected_behaviour: The relationship picker lists grouped relationships; selection updates model.relationship, logs metadata-only diagnostics, and invalidates stale output.
external_evidence_remaining: Direct relationship-picker interaction and search behaviour remain unproved by UI automation.
compatibility_notes: Dedicated picker interaction and any search behavior remain unproved by automation.

user_story: As a user, I want to choose the moment or occasion without facing a giant static grid.
expected_behaviour: The occasion picker supports featured and searchable rows; selection updates occasion, applies automatic careful-treatment policy, logs metadata-only diagnostics, and invalidates stale output.
external_evidence_remaining: Direct occasion-picker and search interaction remain unproved by UI automation.
compatibility_notes: Automatic treatment changes without exposing a writing-mode selector.

user_story: As a user, I want the app to match the stakes without making me understand writing modes.
expected_behaviour: The composer exposes no writing-mode control; ordinary moments retain the default internal mode while sympathy, pet sympathy, and apology align to automatic extra care.
compatibility_notes: Internal compatibility state remains until the planned recovery, routing, prompt, styling, and Pressure Check cleanup; it has no selectable UI.
Removed the dead selector while retaining internal compatibility values required by routing and recovery.

user_story: As a user, I want to enter the real sentence or detail I need to say so the draft is grounded in my words.
expected_behaviour: MomentModel.trueThing maps into MomentInput.trueThing; edits invalidate stale output and refresh local refusal/pressure signals.
compatibility_notes: Drafting remains explicit after detail edits.

user_story: As a user entering an explicit high-risk phrase, I should see immediate support instead of a drafted message.
expected_behaviour: MomentInput.safetySignal matches a narrow explicit phrase list; canDraft becomes false and RoutingMessageWritingService throws contentBlocked before either writing client is called; the UI explains the refusal and presents support actions.
external_evidence_remaining: Locale-aware refusal evidence and human safety review remain open.
known_defects: The defensive block is limited to an English phrase list rather than a general classifier.
compatibility_notes: Keep the scope narrow: this is a defensive refusal path, not a crisis-assessment product. Locale-aware evidence and human review remain open.
The refusal UI now explains why drafting stopped before presenting support resources.

user_story: As a user, I want drafting to start only when I tap Write draft so generation is intentional.
expected_behaviour: MomentModel.startDraft is manual and owns the retained generation task; typing and input selection do not start generation.
compatibility_notes: Stop and broader cancellation behaviour are recorded separately in US-057.

user_story: As a user with an everyday moment, I want a private on-device draft where available.
expected_behaviour: FoundationModelsPrivateDraftClient checks model availability, builds testable standing instructions and prompt components, uses typed generation, and returns a private MomentDraftBundle.
external_evidence_remaining: Writing quality and latency remain unmeasured on an Apple Intelligence-capable physical device.
compatibility_notes: No template fallback exists in the production service; physical-device output and latency remain release evidence.

user_story: As a user, I want an honest unavailable state if private drafting cannot run on my device.
expected_behaviour: FoundationModelsPrivateDraftClient maps availability and generation failures to user-safe GenerationError messages; RoutingMessageWritingService enforces per-lane and total technical deadlines and MomentModel exposes draftUnavailableReason.
external_evidence_remaining: The end-to-end release UX deadline remains to be approved and measured.
compatibility_notes: Provider/model names stay hidden; the measured release UX deadline remains open separately.
Bounded service deadlines cover draft and named adjustments while cancelling the losing operation before fallback.

user_story: As a user with a sensitive moment, I want the app to apply calmer treatment without making me select a writing mode.
expected_behaviour: RoutingMessageWritingService sends occasions that require careful treatment to carefulClient; GatewayCarefulMomentClient uses the provider-neutral gateway contract and records the careful product lane.
external_evidence_remaining: Guarded staging quality and reliability evidence remain open.
compatibility_notes: Careful routing is automatic and independent of Premium billing; PCC remains an optional post-v1 experiment.

user_story: As a user, I want drafting to recover gracefully when the preferred lane is unavailable.
expected_behaviour: Careful failures may fall back to private except contentBlocked; private timedOut/rateLimited/requestNeedsFreshKey/serviceUnavailable/unexpectedResponse may route to careful; offline and usage-limit errors do not silently bypass the private lane.
compatibility_notes: Fallback preserves the typed user-safe error policy and respects the total technical deadline.

user_story: As a user, I want the generated message to read like correspondence, not a chat bubble.
expected_behaviour: MomentSheetView renders selectable draft text on a paper-like content surface with metadata and actions nearby.
external_evidence_remaining: VoiceOver and physical-device presentation evidence remain open.
compatibility_notes: Dynamic Type automation exists; broader accessibility and physical-device release evidence remain separate.

user_story: As a user, I want to make a draft warmer, shorter, or more direct without starting over.
expected_behaviour: MomentAdjustment supports warmer, shorter, and moreDirect; MomentModel.adjust calls the service with current-draft context and stores an undo snapshot.
external_evidence_remaining: Direct adjustment-chip interaction remains unproved by UI automation.
compatibility_notes: Warmer Shorter and Direct share the same behavioral plumbing; none currently has direct chip-interaction automation.

user_story: As a user, I want a more careful rewrite that preserves the current draft as context.
expected_behaviour: The dedicated action, result controls, model entry point, refinement protocol, gateway call, diagnostics trigger, and prompt vocabulary are removed; sensitive treatment is automatic and post-draft rewrites use named adjustments or Another.
compatibility_notes: The historical row remains solely to record the removal.
Removed because the action duplicated occasion-aware care and created a third generation pathway.

feature: Draft edit undo keep history and restart recovery
user_story: As a user, I want to edit, undo, keep, restore, or recover a draft after restart so I can preserve my words and recover if an edit or rewrite lost what I meant.
expected_behaviour: MomentModel stores recoverable draft snapshots before user edits, named draft adjustments, and manual rewrites; restorePreviousDraft pops the latest snapshot; restoreDraftSnapshot(id:) restores a selected history row while preserving earlier snapshots; keepCurrentDraftChange clears the decision; updateActiveDraftMessage edits the active bundle and refreshes local pressure checks; MomentDraftRecoveryStore persists the active draft bundle plus moment fields and snapshot stack locally for the app root; Start over and moment changes clear recovery; MomentDraftHistorySheet lists current-session snapshots with Restore actions. Legacy manual-care lane values decode as the current careful lane and are re-encoded in normalized form.
compatibility_notes: Implemented covers local active draft recovery; saved-draft library remains opt-in via Save.

Added inline active-draft editing, Undo edit / Keep edits controls, recoverable snapshot history, a current-session Draft history sheet, local active-draft recovery across app relaunch, pressure-check refresh when users edit wording, and backward-compatible lane normalization.

user_story: As a user, I want the app to flag wording that may pressure the recipient.
expected_behaviour: PressureCheck.local inspects generated text and trueThing for reassurance, conditional apology, and heaviness phrases; draft bundles merge local pressure notes; the draft pressure card lets the user keep the current draft or use the named Direct adjustment while preserving current-draft context and undo.
external_evidence_remaining: Broader examples, human safety and accessibility review, and physical-device evidence remain open.
known_defects: Pressure Check remains limited by local phrase lists and needs broader copy review.
compatibility_notes: Needs broader examples and safety copy review before this can be marked Implemented. Physical-device and human safety/accessibility evidence remain separate release work.

Pressure Check offers Keep draft and Make direct. Make direct uses the normal named-adjustment lifecycle, keeps the current draft as rewrite context, acknowledges the rewritten finding, and preserves undo.

user_story: As a user, I want to copy the draft for use in another app.
expected_behaviour: Active and saved-draft actions copy the currently visible reviewed text and show acknowledgement only after the copy action runs.
compatibility_notes: Copy does not claim an external paste succeeded; it acknowledges only the local pasteboard action.

user_story: As a user, I want to share the draft using system sharing.
expected_behaviour: Active and saved-draft surfaces expose one destination-neutral SwiftUI ShareLink for the reviewed plain text; opening or cancelling the chooser never records a destination or successful send.
external_evidence_remaining: Physical-device ShareLink destination presentation remains unproved.
compatibility_notes: The system owns destination selection; physical-device ShareLink evidence remains a release gate.
Replaced destination claims and destination telemetry with direct ShareLink and a shared truthful presentation policy.

user_story: As a user, I want saved messages to appear only when I deliberately tap Save.
expected_behaviour: MomentSheetView inserts SavedMomentDraftRecord only from the explicit Save action; generation and recovery do not add a saved-library record.
compatibility_notes: Generated and recovered drafts remain unsaved until the user chooses Save.

user_story: As a user, I want to start over without stale draft state or stale keyboard focus.
expected_behaviour: MomentModel.startNewMoment cancels active generation and resets person, committed-person state, relationship, occasion, compatibility register, trueThing, draft, errors, snapshots, and recovery.
compatibility_notes: The reset cannot allow a late generation result to repopulate the cleared Moment.

user_story: As a user, I want to save a relationship detail for future drafts only when I choose it.
expected_behaviour: MomentMemorySection creates approved RelationshipTruthBeadRecord memory only after the current person is committed and the user submits the detail.
compatibility_notes: No Contacts or Calendar inference occurs; creation is explicitly user-triggered.
Relationship memory now appears after person commit while draft-result UI remains state-gated.

feature: Edit, pause, delete, and explain Truth Beads
user_story: As a user, I want relationship details to stay correct, pausable, deletable, and explainable.
expected_behaviour: RelationshipMemoryDetailView edits person/text/approved state saves with rollback deletes only after confirmation and displays explanatory copy.
compatibility_notes: The retained simulator pass did not tap Delete; deletion integrity is behavioral rather than direct UI proof.

user_story: As a user, I want to save style guidance for a person without treating it as a fact to quote.
expected_behaviour: RelationshipVoiceCardRecord and UI support create, edit, approval toggle, delete, and explain style-only use; approved voice cards are fetched only for the current person and the private-draft prompt labels them as style guidance rather than facts to quote.
compatibility_notes: Voice Card means user-approved writing-style guidance; spoken input is the separate removed/deferred feature in US-049.
Relationship memory is available after the person is committed; prompt construction is now tested through a pure plan rather than source-string assertions.

user_story: As a user, I want to review saved relationship memory in one place.
expected_behaviour: RelationshipMemoryVaultView combines Truth Beads and Voice Cards, sorts by updatedAt, supports search and detail navigation, and routes swipe deletion through confirmation and rollback-safe persistence.
external_evidence_remaining: The list swipe interaction remains unproved by direct UI automation.
compatibility_notes: Do not treat shared SwiftData behaviour as direct UI proof; the swipe gesture itself remains unautomated.

user_story: As a user, I want only approved memory for the current person to influence a draft.
expected_behaviour: SwiftDataRelationshipMemoryProvider uses stable persisted normalized person keys to fetch only approved Truth Beads and Voice Cards for the current person.
compatibility_notes: The normalized key is internal lookup metadata and is omitted from export.
Persisted normalizedPersonName uses en_US_POSIX normalization approved predicates and empty-key repair.

user_story: As a user, I want to find saved drafts and remove ones I no longer need.
expected_behaviour: SavedMomentDraftsView queries every deliberately saved draft and provides real person, occasion, relationship, and message-text search; unsupported status filters are absent; SavedMomentDraftDetailView requires confirmation and persists deletion before dismissing.
compatibility_notes: Failed deletion rolls back and leaves the detail open with an honest error; status filters require a future explicit schema and product decision rather than invented UI.
Removed unsupported status filters and replaced the Kept badge with the truthful Saved label; retained real search without changing the versioned SwiftData schema.

user_story: As a user, I want to reopen a saved draft and copy, share, or delete it.
expected_behaviour: SavedMomentDraftDetailView shows draft content, exposes one Copy and one destination-neutral ShareLink, and confirms deletion before persisting it.
compatibility_notes: Failed deletion keeps the record and detail visible; Share cancellation records no destination or send.
Uses direct SwiftUI ShareLink for text plus confirmed rollback-safe deletion that dismisses only after persistence succeeds.

user_story: As a user, I want to correct a saved draft without deleting and recreating it.
expected_behaviour: SavedMomentDraftDetailView supports Edit, Cancel, and Save; success appears only after persistence and failure rolls back to the last saved text.
compatibility_notes: UI proof used a deterministic saved draft created with --prosepal-use-mock-writing-service.
Added rollback-safe edit persistence and an honest failure notice while retaining the prior saved value.

user_story: As a user, I want account, Premium, writing, privacy, data, support, legal, and about settings in one place.
expected_behaviour: MomentSettingsView renders the current sections and links to plan, account, local-data, support, legal, and about surfaces; export supports Copy JSON and named-file system sharing.
external_evidence_remaining: Live account, subscription, and system-share evidence remain open.
known_defects: The About section still exposes the migration-era Direction value.
compatibility_notes: Partial reflects known user-facing terminology plus live account/payment/system-share evidence rather than a missing Settings shell.

user_story: As a user, I want to sign in with Apple for continuity and support without being forced before purchase.
expected_behaviour: MomentAppleSignInControl requests no unused contact scopes and supplies a cryptographic nonce; MomentAccountModel exchanges the ID token through Supabase Auth, forwards the one-time authorization code to the authenticated Edge Function, persists the opaque Apple credential ID with the Keychain session, checks credential state, and observes revocation.
external_evidence_remaining: System revocation notification handling and TestFlight proof remain open.
compatibility_notes: Staging accepts both approved iOS App IDs; production configuration is unchanged.

2026-07-16 staging evidence: APPLE_TEAM_ID/APPLE_CLIENT_ID/APPLE_KEY_ID/APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY configured, real-device Sign in with Apple succeeded, and revocation material stored via the deployed exchange-apple-token without redeployment.

user_story: As a signed-in user, I want sign-out to clear account and Premium state safely.
expected_behaviour: MomentAccountModel.signOut signs out with the current token when available, clears the persisted session, sets signed-out state, and locks Premium inactive.
external_evidence_remaining: Running-app sign-out progress, failure, retry, and duplicate-prevention behaviour remain unproved.
known_defects: Sign-out lacks a visible progress, duplicate-prevention, failure, and retry lifecycle while remote and local clearing converge.
compatibility_notes: Functional sign-out is implemented; its cross-cutting waiting experience is part of the Partial US-058 finding.

user_story: As a signed-in user, I want to delete my account and local app data from Settings.
expected_behaviour: MomentAccountModel confirms deletion and calls the authenticated delete-user boundary. Server-confirmed deletion runs one coordinated lifecycle reset: account-scoped work is cancelled, the relationship vault (saved drafts and memory) is erased, the Supabase session is cleared, in-memory entitlement state is reset, and the app root clears the current draft, composer input, draft history, active-draft recovery, and pending launch/share payloads, then resets onboarding so the previous Write and Settings views unmount and the app routes to first-run. Failure preserves the account and local data with retry; an indeterminate outcome signs out but keeps local data and never claims success; cancellation produces no success state. Privacy-safe account_deletion_* events cover started, server_confirmed, local_reset_started/succeeded/failed, succeeded, failed, cancelled, and indeterminate.
external_evidence_remaining: A fresh physical-device run against commits 7c0cb2f and a47a705 confirming onboarding reset and no stale local content remains the only outstanding deletion proof.
compatibility_notes: 2026-07-16 staging evidence: real-device account deletion succeeded server-side, and read-only staging verification confirmed no remaining rows in auth.users, apple_credentials, user_usage, user_entitlements, or user-scoped rate-limit records.
The final delete uses abort-bound transport where supported; confirmed and already-deleted results converge while an unconfirmed final commit returns indeterminate.

A 2026-07-15 staging device test showed partial deletion (no onboarding return, generated message still visible, no outcome event); the coordinated reset and account_deletion_* events fix that class of defect, with indeterminate outcomes now preserving local data instead of wiping prematurely.

feature: Paywall product loading and plan selection
user_story: As a user considering Premium, I want available plans, price/period, and terms before purchase.
expected_behaviour: MomentPaywallSheet loads only configured StoreKit product IDs, selects the recommended product when available, exposes plan choice, and shows renewal disclosure plus Terms and Privacy.
external_evidence_remaining: Configured StoreKit products and all direct StoreKit scenarios must execute with zero failures and zero skips on a working runtime.
known_defects: The current StoreKit runtime returns no products for the configured identifiers.
compatibility_notes: Keep Partial until the configured products return and every direct StoreKit scenario executes with zero failures and zero skips.

user_story: As a user, I want to purchase without mandatory app sign-in and unlock only after entitlement is active.
expected_behaviour: StoreKitSubscriptionClient purchases the selected product; cancellation and pending stay locked, and MomentAccountModel unlocks only after verified entitlement convergence.
external_evidence_remaining: Direct StoreKit purchase scenarios and sandbox purchase evidence remain open.
known_defects: The app-hosted StoreKit purchase scenarios cannot execute until the runtime returns configured products.
compatibility_notes: No purchase is claimed complete until StoreKit and entitlement convergence confirm it.

user_story: As a user, I want to restore purchases from both Paywall and Settings.
expected_behaviour: Paywall and Settings call the same restore boundary; active entitlement unlocks, confirmed inactivity stays locked, and failures return a user-safe retry state.
external_evidence_remaining: Active sandbox or TestFlight restore and App Store server reconciliation evidence remain open.
compatibility_notes: Local policy coverage does not substitute for sandbox/TestFlight restore and server reconciliation.

user_story: As a user, I want paid cloud access to match server entitlement rather than stale local UI.
expected_behaviour: App Store notification and reconciliation functions update user_entitlements; the iOS client supplies appAccountToken only for a valid signed-in Supabase UUID.
external_evidence_remaining: Live App Store notification, reconciliation, and paid-gateway ownership evidence remain open in staging or TestFlight.
compatibility_notes: StoreKit is local truth while the server remains authoritative for paid gateway policy and cloud extras.

user_story: As a user, I want support, Terms, Privacy Policy, and app version information accessible from Settings.
expected_behaviour: MomentSettingsView links support email, exposes a copy-support fallback, opens the standard EULA and privacy URL, and shows app version/build; the current About section also exposes a Direction row.
known_defects: The About Direction value says Native iOS even though ProsePal is the only current app.
compatibility_notes: Support and legal actions are implemented; Partial is caused by the known misleading About vocabulary.

user_story: As a user or tester, I want the app to show whether private and careful writing are configured without leaking secrets.
expected_behaviour: NativeRuntimeReadiness exposes configuration booleans; Settings shows Private Draft and automatic Sensitive moments readiness labels.
compatibility_notes: Secret values are not printed and the readiness row is status rather than a manual writing control.

user_story: As a privacy-sensitive user, I want diagnostics to avoid raw message content and secrets.
expected_behaviour: NativeDiagnosticsLogger records structured action names states request prefixes and character counts rather than raw message text credentials or tokens.
compatibility_notes: No third-party analytics SDK is present by default.

user_story: As a signed-in user, I want my session persisted securely between launches.
expected_behaviour: KeychainAuthSessionStore encodes AuthSession, saves to Keychain, loads, updates, and clears by service/account; AuthSessionController owns refresh and replacement races.
external_evidence_remaining: Physical-device Keychain continuity remains release evidence.
compatibility_notes: Physical-device Keychain continuity remains release evidence rather than an unsupported automated claim.

user_story: As a user, I want careful generation errors to be recoverable and user-safe.
expected_behaviour: GatewayMessageWritingClient sends a strict request identity with CardRequest; initial automatic careful drafts persist that identity across ambiguous retries; each named adjustment uses a fresh key for its explicit action; the gateway reserves quota and burst capacity before provider work, safely replays completed duplicates, and propagates client cancellation into the active provider fetch without starting another fallback model.
external_evidence_remaining: Guarded staging generation and replay evidence remain open.
known_defects: Named adjustment requests do not yet have durable request identities.
compatibility_notes: Initial careful drafts survive a lost response without a second charge; durable identities for named Adjust actions plus guarded staging proof remain open.

user_story: As a user, I want to start or resume a Moment from Shortcuts or Siri.
expected_behaviour: StartMomentIntent writes a MomentLaunchRequest and opens a MomentDeepLink from the shared ProsePalDomain handoff contract; App Shortcuts supplies the supported phrases.
external_evidence_remaining: Real Shortcuts and Siri execution on a physical device remain open.
compatibility_notes: Ship only if the actual system surface passes production-like qualification.
Uses the canonical ProsePalDomain launch contract; App Intent surfaces retain only the AppIntents-dependent types.

user_story: As a user, I want a widget for relationship care reminders or glanceable moments.
expected_behaviour: Production and staging WidgetKit extensions embed CareGlanceWidget; its bundle-aware URL opens the matching app into a widget-sourced Moment.
external_evidence_remaining: Widget Gallery configuration and physical-device widget launch remain open.
compatibility_notes: Keep Partial until the widget is configured and launched from the real system surface.
Staging target wiring and bundle-aware handoff were added.
Open URLs are built with MomentDeepLink.momentURL(source:environment:); production/staging scheme routing lives in MomentHandoffEnvironment, not inline in the widget.

user_story: As a user, I want a system control to quickly start a Moment.
expected_behaviour: StartMomentControlWidget is embedded in both widget targets and opens a bundle-aware control_center deep link that the app accepts.
external_evidence_remaining: Real Control Center or Action Button configuration and physical-device launch remain open.
compatibility_notes: Keep Partial until the control is configured and launched from Control Center or the Action Button.
Staging target embedding and bundle-aware URLs were added.
Open URLs are built with MomentDeepLink.momentURL(source:environment:); production/staging scheme routing lives in MomentHandoffEnvironment, not inline in the widget.

user_story: As a user, I want to turn outside text or context into a Moment.
expected_behaviour: Production and staging share extensions accept text/URL providers, sanitise and store capped context in the canonical SharedMomentLaunchPayload/SharedMomentLaunchStore contract keyed per environment, and open the matching app; MomentAppRootView consumes the payload without logging raw content. MomentDeepLink accepts both prosepal and prosepal-staging schemes.
external_evidence_remaining: A complete system Share Extension to app handoff remains unproved.
compatibility_notes: No raw shared content enters the deep-link URL; keep Partial until the real system handoff is captured.
The extension links ProsePalDomain and uses the canonical contract with no target-local payload, store, key, or scheme; production and staging are isolated by per-environment app-group key.

user_story: As a user, I want to say the messy thing by voice instead of typing it.
expected_behaviour: The composer has no voice-entry control and the app declares no microphone or speech-recognition usage descriptions; Moment detail is typed input only.
compatibility_notes: Voice input is deferred as a separately owned post-v1 feature; this row preserves useful removal history without citing a deleted file.
The control model wiring transcriber implementation tests and permission strings were removed from v1.

user_story: As a user, I want to export my local ProsePal data from Settings without waiting for support.
expected_behaviour: RelationshipVaultExporter creates a versioned JSON snapshot of Truth Beads, Voice Cards, and saved drafts; Settings shows counts filename preview Refresh Copy JSON and a named-file ShareLink backed by a typed Transferable.
external_evidence_remaining: Physical-device file-export destination presentation remains unproved.
compatibility_notes: The export omits internal person keys and store paths; account/server export remains separate.
MomentLocalDataExport preserves the generated filename and exact bytes cleans temporary files and retains Copy JSON.

user_story: As a user, I want local relationship memory to be stored privately and erased safely when deleting my account.
expected_behaviour: The vault uses SwiftData in a backup-excluded Application Support directory, falls back to an honest ephemeral vault if persistence cannot open, and erases Truth Beads Voice Cards saved drafts and fallback files during local cleanup.
known_defects: A non-failing Core Data NSXPCConnection warning may appear during package tests.
compatibility_notes: At-rest encryption beyond Apple data protection remains a separate post-v1 decision.
Persistent-or-ephemeral startup local erasure fallback-file cleanup and a visible persistence status are implemented.

user_story: As a user, I should not see provider or model names in the app UI.
expected_behaviour: UI depends on MessageWritingService and describes automatic Sensitive moments readiness without provider/model names or a manual careful-writing action.
compatibility_notes: Automated guards fail if provider/model names or the retired manual-care action drift into App or ProsePalUI source.

user_story: As a user using accessibility settings, I want controls, text, navigation, and progress states to remain usable.
expected_behaviour: SwiftUI surfaces use labels selectable text standard navigation reduce-motion checks accessible progress values explicit icon labels an accessibility-size composer variant inline draft actions and opaque Reduce Transparency fallbacks.
external_evidence_remaining: VoiceOver, Switch Control, broader large-text flows, and physical-device accessibility evidence remain open.
compatibility_notes: Keep Partial until VoiceOver Switch Control broader large-text flows and physical-device evidence pass.
Accessibility-size chrome inline actions wrapping and Reduce Transparency surfaces were added.

user_story: As a user, I want the iOS app to stay dependency-light and privacy-safe by default.
expected_behaviour: Package.swift has no package dependencies; the client uses StoreKit SwiftData Foundation Models and provider-neutral HTTP boundaries without RevenueCat Firebase AI or provider SDKs.
compatibility_notes: Provider-neutral server calls do not require a provider SDK in the app.

user_story: As a purchaser, I want Premium to follow verified StoreKit truth without leaking across accounts or disappearing during a temporary store outage.
expected_behaviour: StoreKitSubscriptionClient returns explicit active confirmed-inactive or unknown state; MomentAccountModel keeps same-account last-known-good active access during transient unknown state, clears it on confirmed inactivity or account switch, enforces appAccountToken compatibility, and finishes purchases or updates only after matching convergence.
external_evidence_remaining: All direct StoreKit scenarios must execute without skips; sandbox or TestFlight and server-ownership evidence remain open.
known_defects: The current StoreKit runtime returns an empty successful product lookup, which is a setup failure rather than a skippable Apple runtime error.
compatibility_notes: Keep Partial until all direct StoreKit scenarios execute without skips and sandbox/TestFlight plus server ownership evidence pass.
Added tri-state entitlement policy, renewal-state mapping, ownership and account-epoch rules, deferred finish/redelivery, explicit retired-product recognition, and direct SKTestSession scenarios
The app-hosted suite defines 12 direct StoreKit scenarios, and its release gate requires zero failures and zero skips.

user_story: As a release owner, I want durable user journeys exercised in the running iOS app so broken wiring cannot pass on source assertions alone.
expected_behaviour: A focused XCUITest target drives isolated first-run navigation generation delayed authentication and subscription work account-deletion outcomes persistence generic sharing/export and accessibility-size scenarios through real actions and stable accessibility contracts.
external_evidence_remaining: Live Apple authorization, StoreKit sandbox transactions, provider output, VoiceOver, generic share destinations, and physical-device behaviour remain external release evidence.
known_defects: Sign-out progress and paywall-local purchase or restore outcome presentation remain product findings.
compatibility_notes: Local automation is not represented as proof of live Apple provider accessibility or physical-device behavior.
DEBUG-only named scenarios provide delayed success and failure boundaries without changing release behavior.

user_story: As a user waiting for a draft, I want Stop and navigation changes to end obsolete work without losing my input or allowing a late result to appear.
expected_behaviour: MomentModel alone owns the retained generation task; Stop reset meaning-bearing input changes composer dismissal app backgrounding and superseding work cancel it while a generation identity suppresses late results.
compatibility_notes: The UI exposes Stop only while generation is active; cancellation never claims a draft was completed.

user_story: As a user starting durable network-backed work, I want immediate honest feedback and protection from accidental duplicate submission.
expected_behaviour: Generation sign-in product loading purchase restore and account deletion expose indeterminate progress disable or remove duplicate actions preserve writing and reveal confirmed success failure retry or indeterminate outcomes without fake percentages.

user_story: As a user considering or reaching a writing limit, I want policy claims to match the server rather than invented counters reset dates or unlimited promises.
expected_behaviour: Plan and Paywall promise more drafts and refines through higher writing limits; the limit state preserves the gateway user-safe message and never invents counters reset dates meters or unlimited access. One completed unique gateway request consumes one allowance while private on-device work failures and replay do not.
compatibility_notes: The finite 500-per-month entitled repository policy remains an explicit release-owner decision before any numerical customer promise; the current UI stays non-quantified.

Replaced unsupported unlimited language and infinity glyphs across the app and active design sources; documented the request-ledger counting contract and retained exact quota copy behind an owner approval gate.

user_story: As a user, I want to choose the voice of the message before generation.
expected_behaviour: The composer exposes every Tone case in one menu; selection updates the meaning-bearing Moment state invalidates stale output persists through recovery and reaches both private and gateway prompt contracts.

user_story: As a user, I want to choose a brief standard or detailed message before generation.
expected_behaviour: The composer exposes Brief Standard and Detailed controls; selection updates meaning-bearing Moment state invalidates stale output persists through recovery and reaches both writing lanes as a generation hint.
external_evidence_remaining: Direct message-length control interaction remains unproved by UI automation.
compatibility_notes: Standard is the default; each label maps to a stable sentence-count hint rather than a fake exact guarantee.

user_story: As a user, I want spelling and locale behavior to follow my device without another setup control.
expected_behaviour: MomentInput and CardIntent derive Locale.current.identifier and the automatic spelling preference by default; both private and gateway prompts receive the locale while the composer exposes no redundant spelling picker.
compatibility_notes: Locale handling is automatic product behavior not a hidden user preference.

user_story: As a user, I want another way to say the same Moment without losing the draft I already have.
expected_behaviour: The result rail exposes Another; MomentModel.rewriteDraft sends the same meaning-bearing Moment through the model-owned draft lifecycle and replaces the active bundle only after success while storing the previous wording as a recoverable rewrite snapshot.
external_evidence_remaining: Direct Another replacement, undo, and chip interaction remain unproved by UI automation.
compatibility_notes: Another is a fresh draft request rather than a named tone or length adjustment; the current one-draft result model remains in place until the planned three-option flow is delivered.
